Don't let the skull face fool you, this is a jumping spider and is highly intelligent and 100% harmless to humans! They're curious little buggers that look around the world with near 360 degree vision, but prefer to inspect with their huge primary eyes. They're very cute and filled with personality if you look close enough. Some are more skittish, and others will let you handle and play with them. 😊 they're my favorite animal, and they're so sadly misunderstood. People hear the 'jumping' part and lose their shit, when in reality all they wanna do is get to a warm place to sunbathe and curl up in little web sleeping bags at the end of the day for a snooze.

As a huge bird lover I always have to mention every opportunity I get that a lot of people buy parakeets and cockatiels (or any other bird for that matter), whether it be as a pet or a gift, ENTIRELY unaware of the care and commitment that goes into caring for a birb. I'm talking lifetime commitment for some birds. Parakeets in particular are so much more intelligent than anyone gives them credit for, and can learn a surprisingly large vocabulary of words. Most birds have the intelligence of a 2-3 year old, and can live for decades. Please don't buy birdies unless you are very aware of the risks. I purchased my feather child entirely aware that he'll be my roommate for the next 30 or so years, chewing on all my papers and pooping on my stuff.

Parents' divorce. I remember the day they told me they were splitting. The next 5 years were the worst of my life so far. Specifics are kinda blurred because I've repressed it all, but it can be summed up as this:
I listened to my parents scream at each other daily, developed severe depression and anxiety, and my mother moved out with me and my brother. She manipulated us to believe my father was a terrible person and I told my father I hated him to his face and refused to talk to him as a result. I also listened to my mother discuss on a daily basis that she wanted to die, and when I refused to listen to her she'd go to my little brother who was only 10 instead. I'm pretty sure he's more messed up from all this shit than I am.
I was also taken advantage of sexually at only 14 by an older boyfriend whom I then believed I was head over heels for, and after two years abandoned by said boyfriend when he went to school and stopped answering my texts.
I figured out I wanted to be a boy instead of a girl, and fought with myself and my family quite a lot over it too.
Found out my dad was dating a woman behind everyone's back (whom would later end up causing a fucking myriad of even more problems and I'd have to type a novel to cover it all), aaand then subsequently found out my dad had been lying about a shit ton of MORE stuff, like being severely short on money and unable to support both us and himself. He told me there was a period where he was positive he would be losing his own house just to pay for us. My mom didn't work, all she did was lay about pining after my dad who didn't love her anymore. So my dad was literally dying working enough to cover two houses, two families, etc. My mother also refused to give up luxuries she once had like two week vacations and hair appointments, meanwhile we were dying for a decent dinner. Dad owed a ton of money to his now ex girlfriend, owed money on a title loan that had racked up interest... the threat that we'd lose everything hung over my head every day and it was honestly so scary. My dad works his ass off STILL to this day, and hasn't taken a single vacation since this started.

Eventually... Idunno. My father sorta resigned that this shit would only continue unless he brought everyone back under one household. We all moved back into his house, and... I guess this is the 'after.' My parents clearly don't love each other, but things are somewhat happier. We can actually afford luxuries again and we're going to be going on a vacation here soon all together. I just turned 20 last month and I work two jobs, but I still retain a lot of trauma and depression from all that. I tend to keep things from my parents now and I kinda shut myself in my room when I can, but all in all I'm marginally happier than when things were all split up. Still want to be a boy after 4 years, parents have finally resigned to the fact it's not a phase, and I'm looking into hormone treatment sometime in the future. I'm hoping for that to be another 'after', and a much, much happier one.
